generatedProse.concept-context: In psychology, excelling means more than a strong mark in your modules. Alongside the grade sits your development as a thinker: growing more curious about why people behave as they do, more careful with evidence, and more independent in how you read studies. A student who earns a good grade and also becomes a sharper, more questioning psychologist has excelled more fully than one who earns the grade alone.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two psychology students on the same first-year module.

Tom has one aim: the highest mark possible. He learns exactly what the marker wants, revises precisely that, and is pleased with a strong grade. The mark is real, but nothing else has changed. Tom is no more curious about psychology than before, and has little interest in the ideas beyond the assessment. This is success measured only as academic performance.

Amara wants to do well too, but also wants to understand the subject and become a better thinker. She reads around the topic, follows up studies that are not strictly needed for the mark, and finishes the module more confident and more interested in psychology than before. Her grade is good, and she has grown as well. This is excelling: academic performance and personal development together.

Both students passed well. Only Amara treated the module as a chance to grow, not just a grade to earn.
generatedProse.summary: Excelling in psychology means more than a high mark. Success has two sides: academic performance, the grades and skills, and personal development, the way you grow as a thinker through the subject. Excelling is a mindset you bring, not a fixed trait. You can now define excelling in this fuller way and recognise the mindset behind it. The next lesson looks at the growth mindset and self-belief that make it possible.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's approach closer to excelling?

items.text: She earned a good grade and also grew more confident and interested in psychology.
She earned a higher grade than Tom did.
She spent far longer on the module than Tom did.
She focused only on what the marker wanted.

feedback.correct: That's right. Amara scored well and grew as a thinker, which is excelling.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what Amara gained beyond the grade.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara excelled because she grew in confidence and interest as well as scoring well, not because of a higher grade or more time.
